tools/check_public_pii.py::mask_heredoc_: Drops `out.append(chr(10))` in the body/delimiter path. mask_heredoc_bodies exists to guarantee ONE property: a heredoc body yields no write targets. Its output is consumed only by the redirect / tee / sed -i / dd-of regexes, all of which need `>` , `tee`, `-i` or `of=` to match. The values appended at these sites are a newline, a single space, a heredoc delimiter (matched by [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*), or the literal `<<DELIM` marker -- NONE of which contains `>` or any redirect token. Every body character has already been replaced by a space, so no `>` survives in that region for a dropped character to abut. Dropping these calls therefore only REMOVES characters from the masked filler; it cannot ADD redirect syntax, so the extracted target set is provably identical. Equivalent mutant, by argument rather than by assumption. The mutants in this function that were NOT equivalent were killed rather than allowlisted: quote-state tracking (3 killed by test_mask_does_not_treat_a_QUOTED_heredoc_marker_as_a_heredoc and siblings), mid-line delimiter lookalikes (killed by test_mask_does_not_close_the_heredoc_mid_line_on_a_delimiter_lookalike), and quote closing (killed by test_mask_closes_quotes_so_a_later_heredoc_is_still_detected). 12 survivors -> 6. 2026-08-24.

tools/check_table_integrity.py::scan_fil: UNREACHABLE through the shipped entry points, per the HOOK_AUTHORING diagnosis order (weak assertion -> self-consistency -> unreachable -> equivalent). Reaching it needs a path where is_file() is True but read_text() still raises: a permissions or unlink race. That cannot be constructed portably in CI (it needs a chmod/root-owned file, and CI often runs as root, where chmod 000 does not deny). Dropping the continue leaves `text` unbound, so the NameError propagates to the outer fail-open and exits 0 -- the same silent no-op the guard already produces for an unreadable file. Kept as defence-in-depth against a future edit that moves the read out of the try.

Observable behaviour is byte-identical. The explicit check is kept so the common case (file simply absent) does not depend on exception control flow.

It survives because pytest already puts the repo on sys.path, so the import succeeds either way inside the suite. Dropping it would fall through to `from inbox_lock import ...` and die with a NameError/ImportError instead of exit 3 -- a worse message on a path that is already fatal, and still incapable of touching a frame.

Drops the `print(json.dumps(...))` in the ImportError guard for a missing PyYAML. Reachable only when PyYAML is absent, which is never true in the test environment because the suite itself imports yaml. HONEST NOTE: this IS testable -- a subprocess run with a sitecustomize shim that hides `yaml` would exercise it -- so this is allowlisted for cost, not impossibility. Accepted because the guard is a startup diagnostic on a path where the tool cannot run at all; it neither reads nor writes a frame, so no mutation of it can produce a wrong frame.

tools/meeting_vocab.py::_named_speaker_t: `if not owner and not other: return None` after the split loop. Reaching it requires every body behind a >=3-occurrence label to be empty, which no real transcript produces and which the earlier speaker-frequency floor makes vanishingly unlikely. `if len(parts) < 3: return None` after the speaker set is established. Unreachable by construction: the function has already required two distinct labels each matching _NAMED_TURN_RE at least three times, so the same regex splitting the same text cannot yield fewer than three parts. tools/meeting_vocab.py::split_transcript: `if len(parts) < 3: return [], []` is an early-exit guard for text with no recognised speaker label. Forcing it false does not change the result: _TURN_RE.split() on unlabelled text returns a 1-element list, so the loop below runs `range(1, 0, 2)`, which is empty, and the function returns the same ([], []) by falling through. Proven equivalent rather than assumed: test_unlabelled_text_returns_two_empty_lists_not_a_crash asserts that exact return and passes with the mutant applied, which is what identifies it as equivalent instead of uncovered. The guard is kept for readability, and because it makes the parse-failure contract explicit at the top of the function where a reader looks for it. The OTHER survivor in this function (`if not body:`) was NOT allowlisted - it was killed by test_empty_turn_bodies_are_skipped_not_counted_as_turns. 2026-08-24.

tools/promotion_schema.py::parse_frontma: Drops the `continue` in that same blank/comment branch, which is the other half of the mutant above and equivalent for the same reason: control falls through to a regex that provably cannot match a blank or comment line, then hits the `if not m: continue` on the following branch and skips the line anyway. Note the sibling DROP_CONTINUE, after `if not m`, was NOT allowlisted: dropping that one dereferences None, and it is killed by test_a_non_key_value_line_is_skipped_without_crashing. 2026-08-25.

The blank/comment skip in parse_frontmatter is a pure short-circuit, and the mutant is equivalent by argument rather than by assumption. Forcing the condition False sends blank and comment lines on to the key regex, ^\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*:, which requires a letter or underscore as the first non-space character. A blank line offers none, and a comment line offers '#', so neither can match and both fall to the same `continue` on the next branch. There is no input for which skipping early and matching-then-failing produce different dicts. The guard is kept because it states the intent (comments are not keys) at the site a future edit to the regex would otherwise silently break. 2026-08-25.
